public_rationale: A February 2025 study identifies obstacles to predicting downstream accuracy from scale [e1]. An October 2024 version of another study reports successful preregistered predictions for subsequently released models on selected tasks [e2]. A June 2024 study predicts average downstream error using smaller experiments [e3]. These results establish neither that a generally dependable sizing method was unavailable in June 2025 nor that a validated method could determine sufficient size for arbitrary specified problems [e1, e2, e3].
limitations: Selected-task forecasts and average-error predictions do not establish reliable success on an arbitrary individual problem.
The packet lacks a comprehensive assessment of methods available by June 2025.
The claim leaves sufficient success and whether probabilistic forecasts count as knowing undefined.

evidence.explanation: The study identifies obstacles to predicting downstream accuracy from scale. It does not establish that all possible advance methods fail or that none existed by the post.

Successful prospective predictions challenge a reading that denies all advance knowledge. They predict selected task performance using capability measurements, rather than guaranteeing a sufficient parameter count for an arbitrary individual problem.
The study predicts average downstream error using smaller experiments. This is useful advance information, but an average error prediction does not certify success on any specified problem.
